==English==

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:af|inter-|national|tree=1}}
From {{af|en|inter-|national}}. Introduced in modern English by {{w|Jeremy Bentham}} in his ''[[s:An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation|An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation]]'', 1780.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˌɪn.təˈnæʃ.(ə.)n(ə)l/|[ˌɪntəˈnæʃ(ə)n(ə)ɫ]|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˌɪn.(t)ɚˈnæʃ.(ə.)n(ə)l/|[ˌɪntɚˈnæʃ(ə)n(ə)ɫ]|[ˌɪɾ̃ɚˈnæʃ(ə)n(ə)ɫ]|a=GenAm}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-international.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|æʃənəl|s=5}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj|abbr=int'l,intl,intl.}}

# Of or having to do with more than one [[nation]].
## Between or among nations.
##: {{ux|en|an '''international''' discussion}}
## Participated in by two or more nations.
##: {{ux|en|an '''international''' competition}}
##* {{RQ:en:CNN|date=2025-02-20|author=Homero De la Fuente|title=Canada beats Team USA in overtime thriller to win hockey’s first-ever 4 Nations Face-off championship|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/02/20/sport/4-nations-face-off-championship-spt
|passage=Canada’s men’s hockey team defeated the USA 3-2 in overtime Thursday to capture the inaugural 4 Nations Face-Off Championship as the NHL put on a show in the first edition of this midseason '''international''' tournament.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250328111917/https://www.cnn.com/2025/02/20/sport/4-nations-face-off-championship-spt/}}
## {{U|common}} to, or [[affecting]], two or more nations.
##: {{ux|en|an '''international''' rule}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1780|year_published=1789|author=w:Jeremy Bentham|title=w:An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation|chapter=[[s:An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation/Preface|Preface]]|url=https://www.koeblergerhard.de/Fontes/BenthamJeremyMoralsandLegislation1789.pdf|page=6|brackets=1
|passage=Principles of legiſlation in matters betwixt nation and nation, or, to uſe a new though not inexpreſſive appellation, in matters of '''''international''''' law.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260105000841/https://www.koeblergerhard.de/Fontes/BenthamJeremyMoralsandLegislation1789.pdf}}
## Serving two or more nations.
##: {{ux|en|an '''international''' airport}}
# Of or concerning the association called the International.
# Independent of national [[boundaries]]; common to all people.
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-07|author=w:Joseph Stiglitz
|volume=188|issue=26|page=19|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/2013/may/27/globalisation-is-about-taxes-too|title=Globalisation is about taxes too
|passage=It is time the '''international''' community faced the reality: we have an unmanageable, unfair, distortionary global tax regime. It is a tax system that is pivotal in creating the increasing inequality that marks most advanced countries today – with America standing out in the forefront and the UK not far behind.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013204907/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2013/may/27/globalisation-is-about-taxes-too|archivedate=13 October 2026}}
#: {{ux|en|The atmosphere is an '''international''' resource.}}
#: {{ux|en|the '''international''' community of scholars}}
# {{U|foreign}}; of another nation.
#: {{ux|en|an '''international''' student}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|sports|chiefly|Britain|Ireland|AU}} Someone who has represented their country in a particular sport.
#: {{ux|en|The United team includes five England '''internationals'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Doyle Poison Belt|passage="The young fellah meant no real harm. After all, he's an '''International''', so if he takes half an hour to describe a game of football he has more right to do it than most folk."}}
# {{lb|en|sports|chiefly Britain, Ireland|AU}} A game or contest between two or more nations.
# {{lb|en|politics}} A [[transnational]] [[organization]] of [[political party|political parties]] of similar [[ideology]].
